questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate passive form of the given sentence.**

How much monthly rent did you pay for the house?

options.text: How much monthly rent was paid for the house?
How much monthly rent is being paid for the house?
How much monthly rent was being paid for the house?
How much monthly rent is paid for the house?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. How much monthly rent was paid for the house?**

 
• While changing the active voice into passive voice the **tense** remains the **same**.
 
• Hence, options 2 and option 4 cannot be the answer.
 
• Moreover, being is used in continuous tenses, so, option 3) is also wrong.
 
• Option 1) is correct because it follows all the rules.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.**

She said, "Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate."

options.text: She said that Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak was slipping when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak has slipped when he was trying to skate.
She said that Deepak had slipped when he was trying to skate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e *She said that Deepak slipped when he was trying to skate.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25cf3443523bdade9b54eae0f44214d7fb9974cacdd0708b2812ee08d9a34014.png] **__Explanation:__**

__
 
• While changing direct speech into indirect speech change in the tense will not occur when the time clause is mentioned ('when')
 
• Reporting speech and reported speech are joined with that if the given sentence is a simple sentence.
 
• These rules are followed in option 1) making it the correct answer.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In complex sentences, the past simple and past continuous may remain unchanged if the temporal relationship between the events in the clauses is clear from the context. Examples: 
 
 
• Bill: I was reading a book when I heard the crash.

 Bill said that he was reading a book when he heard the crash.
 
• John: When I got home, I went to bed straight away.

 John told me that when he got home he went to bed straight away.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• So, the correct sentence will be: **The soldiers had no choice but to obey the commander.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• **The error lies in the wrong usage of the Subject-verb agreement**.
 
• Here, the subject is 'number' which is singular must be followed by singular verb 'was' instead of 'were'.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is** 'The number of visitors at the fair **was **much larger than expected'.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. They have no mind of their own.

B. It is misleading to imagine that computers can think like humans.

C. However, they make it possible for people to accumulate thoughts.

D. They cannot do so.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The answer does not begin with sentences A & D because they are dependent sentences. In sentence A & D, we do not know what the word 'they' is talking about.
 
• The answer does not begin with sentence C because a paragraph cannot begin with an adverb.
 
• Therefore, the first sentence begins with B which says 'it is misleading' which means there is a contradict opinion that computers can think like humans' which is given in sentence D that they cannot do so. 
 
• Sentence A is the third sentence as it is continuing why computers cannot think like humans.
 
• The concluding opinion is given in sentence C.
 
• **Therefore, the correct sequence BDAC is followed by Option 1.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Children are the most adversely affected.

B. Their eyesight goes weak from their very childhood.

C. Watching television continuously is very harmful for the eyes.

D. This debilitating effect on eyes results in severe headaches as well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. CABD.**

 
• The only independent sentence from the given sentences is **'C'**, hence, it will be the first sentence.
 
• Sentence 'A' will follow the sentence 'C' because in the sentence 'C' it is being said that watching television is harmful and the sentence 'A', it is being said that who are most affected by it.
 
• In the sentence 'B' pronoun 'their' has been used for 'children' hence, sentence 'B' will follow the sentence 'A'.
 
• so, the last sentence will be 'D'.
 
• Hence, the correct sequence will be: CABD

questions.question:
**Identify the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required, select No substitution.**

No other man in the city is __as rich than he is__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. as rich as he.**

 
• In the given sentence 'as rich than he is' is used which is wrong because we cannot use **'than' **with **as**.
 
• **'as-as'** is used for comparison, hence, **'as rich as he'** is the correct answer.
 
• We cannot use 'so much rich' because so and much both are used for comparison and we cannot use both of them in a sentence.
 
• **more richer** is also wrong because both of them are used for comparison.
